Experimental validation, however, lags far behind bioinformatic prediction, and researchers caution that sponge effects require specific abundance ratios that may exist only in certain cellular contexts. Nevertheless, the ceRNA model provides a unifying language for describing cross-talk among transcript classes and continues to guide the discovery of diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic candidates.
vocab: توان‌بالا؛ فناوری‌های پردازش موازی انبوه نمونه‌ها
RNA بلند غیرکدکننده؛ رونوشت >۲۰۰ نوکلئوتید بدون ساخت پروتئین
RNA درون‌زاد رقیب؛ مدل اسفنجی رقابت بر سر miRNA
اسفنج مولکولی؛ مولکولی که miRNA را به خود می‌گیرد
آزاد از سرکوب؛ بیان مجدد پس از رفع مهار
گذار اپیتلیال-مزانشیمی؛ گام کلیدی تهاجم و متاستاز

questions.q: 1. The primary purpose of the passage is to:
options: prove that lncRNAs are translated into proteins
introduce the ceRNA hypothesis and describe its relevance and limitations in breast cancer research
list all miRNAs expressed in breast cancer
questions.explanation: ساختار متن: معرفی lncRNA → توضیح مدل ceRNA → داده‌های سرطان پستان → محدودیت‌ها → جمع‌بندی. هدفِ «معرفی + نقش + محدودیت» در گزینه ۲ بازتاب کامل دارد.
questions.tip: سوال purpose/ساختار: پاسخ باید «کل» متن را پوشش دهد؛ گزینه‌هایی که فقط یک پاراگراف را می‌پوشانند یا با متن تناقض دارند حذف می‌شوند.

questions.q: 2. According to the ceRNA hypothesis, an oncogenic mRNA is de-repressed when:
options: the miRNA that targets it is sequestered by a competing lncRNA
the lncRNA is degraded by the miRNA
the mRNA acquires new miRNA response elements
questions.explanation: جمله کلیدی: «lncRNAs ... act as molecular sponges, sequestering miRNAs away from their natural mRNA targets» → miRNA که سرکوب‌کننده mRNA انکوژنیک بود، توسط lncRNA به دام می‌افتد و mRNA آزاد می‌شود.
questions.tip: سوالات مکانیسم/علت-مععلول: زنجیره رویداد را با فلش در حاشیه بنویسید: lncRNA ← miRNA ← mRNA آزاد.

questions.q: 3. The phrase "lags far behind" in the last paragraph suggests that:
options: experimental confirmation is much less advanced than computational prediction
researchers refuse to validate the hypothesis
questions.explanation: lag behind = عقب‌ماندن؛ بین prediction (انبوه) و validation (کم) شکاف وجود دارد. گزینه ۳ و ۴ اطلاعات خارج از متن‌اند.
questions.tip: عبارات مقایسه‌ای (lag behind, far behind) معمولاً مقایسه دو چیز در متن را می‌سنجند — دو طرف مقایسه را پیدا کنید.

questions.q: 4. The author mentions the requirement of "specific abundance ratios" in order to:
options: strengthen the claim that all ceRNA interactions are universal
qualify the ceRNA hypothesis by noting context-dependent limitations
questions.explanation: این جمله در دل «researchers caution that...» آمده → کارکرد محدودسازی/احتیاط علمی (qualification). گزینه ۱ واژه universal را اضافه می‌کند و گزینه ۴ با ادامه متن (continues to guide) تناقض دارد.
questions.tip: دقت کنید جمله‌های حاوی caution/however/nevertheless معمولاً «محدودیت» اضافه می‌کنند؛ طراح سوال می‌پرسد چرا نویسنده این را آورده.

questions.q: 5. Which pathway is explicitly named as a convergence point of the predicted axes?
questions.explanation: «converge on key pathways such as PI3K-AKT signaling, EMT, and apoptosis». سه گزینه دیگر مسیرهای معتبر دیگرند اما در متن ذکر نشده‌اند — تله دانش قبلی.
questions.tip: در سوالات explicitly named/stated، فقط به متن رجوع کنید؛ دانش قبلی شما درباره مسیرهای دیگر منشأ خطاست.

readings.title: Functional Analysis of miRNA Data: Bioinformatic Tools
readings.source: بر اساس مقاله: Computational Methods and Software Tools for Functional Analysis of miRNA Data (Biomolecules, 2020)
readings.passage: Because a single microRNA can regulate hundreds of target genes, and a single gene may be regulated by dozens of microRNAs, interpreting miRNA expression data poses a formidable analytical challenge. MicroRNAs rarely act in isolation; instead, they operate within coordinated regulatory networks. To extract biological meaning from lists of differentially expressed miRNAs, researchers rely heavily on enrichment analysis. This family of methods asks whether genes associated with a particular biological term—such as a pathway, molecular function, or disease—are over-represented among the targets of the observed miRNAs compared with what would be expected by chance. The statistical foundation of most enrichment tools is the hypergeometric distribution, often coupled with correction for multiple hypothesis testing, such as the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure, which controls the false discovery rate. Despite their utility, target-prediction algorithms suffer from high false-positive rates, since miRNA targeting depends not only on seed complementarity but also on target-site accessibility, RNA-binding proteins, and cellular context. Consequently, integrated platforms now combine several prediction databases, incorporate experimentally validated interactions from resources such as TarBase, and allow users to filter results by expression consistency. Reviewers of these tools emphasize that the choice of background gene set—the universe of genes against which enrichment is computed—profoundly influences the outcome, and that an inappropriate background can generate entirely spurious conclusions. Careful experimental design and domain knowledge therefore remain indispensable even in the era of one-click bioinformatics.
vocab: آنالیز غنای ژنی؛ آزمون فراوانی غیرتصادفی مقوله‌های بیولوژیک
توزیع فوق‌هندسی؛ مبنای آماری آزمون غنا
نرخ کشف کاذب؛ کنترل خطای آزمون‌های متعدد
مکمل‌بودن ناحیه seed میکروRNA با هدف
مجموعه ژن‌های زمینه برای مقایسه در آزمون غنا

questions.q: 1. Why is interpreting miRNA data described as a "formidable challenge"?
options: because miRNAs act completely independently of each other
because of the many-to-many relationship between miRNAs and their target genes
because miRNAs are too long to sequence
because expression data cannot be measured
questions.explanation: جمله اول: یک miRNA صدها هدف و یک ژن ده‌ها miRNA دارد → رابطه many-to-many. گزینه ۱ دقیقاً برعکس متن (in isolation را متن رد می‌کند) است.
questions.tip: صفت‌های قوی مثل formidable همیشه با دلیل در جمله بعدی همراه‌اند — دلیل را پیدا کنید.

questions.q: 2. The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure is mentioned as a method for:
questions.explanation: «...correction for multiple hypothesis testing, such as the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure, which controls the false discovery rate» — همان جمله تعریف را می‌دهد.
questions.tip: اسامی خاص (روش/دانشمند) معمولاً در سوال با کارکردشان پرسیده می‌شوند؛ جمله حاوی نام را کامل بخوانید.

questions.q: 3. According to the passage, target prediction has high false-positive rates because:
options: targeting also depends on site accessibility, RNA-binding proteins, and cellular context
miRNAs do not bind to mRNAs
questions.explanation: «...since miRNA targeting depends not only on seed complementarity but also on target-site accessibility, RNA-binding proteins, and cellular context» — گزینه ۱ با متن (seed مهم است اما کافی نیست) تناقض دارد.
questions.tip: عبارت not only...but also ساختار «دلیل چندبخشی» می‌سازد؛ گزینه درست همه اجزا را دارد، گزینه انحرافی فقط یک جزء مطلق‌سازی‌شده.

questions.q: 4. The author's attitude toward "one-click bioinformatics" can best be described as:
questions.explanation: جمله پایانی: ابزارها مفیدند اما «careful experimental design and domain knowledge ... remain indispensable» → احتیاط همراه با پذیرش فایده (cautiously skeptical). hostile/indifferent با لحن متن نمی‌خوانند.
questions.tip: سوالات لحن/نگرش (attitude/tone): به قیدها و جمله آخر توجه کنید؛ واژه‌هایی چون remain indispensable نشان‌دهنده موضع میانه-احتیاطی است.

questions.q: 5. All of the following are stated about the background gene set EXCEPT:
options: an inappropriate background can lead to spurious conclusions
it should always include every gene in the genome
it is the universe of genes used for comparison
questions.explanation: متن تعریف و اهمیت پس‌زمینه را گفته اما هرگز گفته «باید همه ژنوم باشد» — این ادعا اضافه‌شده است (EXCEPT).
questions.tip: در سوالات EXCEPT، سه گزینه paraphrase مستقیم متن‌اند؛ گزینه دارای قید مطلق (always/every) معمولاً جواب است.

readings.title: Early Detection of Breast Cancer: Principles of Screening
readings.source: بر اساس کتاب: Early Diagnosis and Treatment of Cancer: Breast Cancer (Saunders/Elsevier)
readings.passage: The rationale for early detection of breast cancer rests on a simple observation: tumors confined to the breast are associated with substantially better survival than tumors that have already spread to regional lymph nodes or distant organs. Screening aims to detect a disease in its preclinical phase—that is, before it produces symptoms—through the systematic application of a test to an apparently healthy population. For a screening program to be justified, several criteria should be satisfied: the disease must be an important health problem with a recognizable early stage; early treatment must offer a benefit over late treatment; and the test must be acceptable, safe, affordable, and sufficiently accurate. Mammography, the reference screening modality, reduces breast cancer mortality in women invited to screening by roughly 20 percent, although debate persists regarding overdiagnosis—the detection of indolent tumors that would never have become clinically apparent. Supplemental screening with magnetic resonance imaging is recommended for women at high genetic risk, such as BRCA mutation carriers, whose dense breast tissue and earlier disease onset reduce mammographic sensitivity. Clinical breast examination and breast self-examination, once promoted widely, now play a limited role because randomized trials failed to demonstrate a mortality reduction. Risk-stratified screening, in which the intensity and modality of surveillance are tailored to individual risk profiles—incorporating polygenic scores, mammographic density, and family history—represents the emerging paradigm, shifting the field from a one-size-fits-all approach toward personalized detection strategies.
vocab: فاز پیش‌بالینی؛ مرحله قبل از بروز علائم
شیوع vs. بروز (تعداد کل موارد در مقابل موارد جدید)
تشخیص بیش‌ازحد؛ کشف تومورهای کم‌خطر که هرگز علامت‌دار نمی‌شدند
تراکم ماموگرافی؛ بافت پستانی که حساسیت تصویربرداری را کم می‌کند
کاهش مرگ‌ومیر؛ معیار اصلی موفقیت غربالگری
امتیاز پلی‌ژنیک؛ مجموع وزن‌دار واریانت‌های ریسک

questions.q: 1. According to the passage, the fundamental justification for early detection is that:
options: localized tumors have considerably better outcomes than disseminated ones
screening eliminates the need for treatment
questions.explanation: جمله اول: «tumors confined to the breast are associated with substantially better survival...» — گزینه‌های مطلق‌سازی‌شده (all/eliminates/no) با متن نمی‌خوانند.
questions.tip: گزینه‌های دارای all/never/no/eliminate تقریباً همیشه غلط‌اند مگر متن صریحاً بگوید.

questions.q: 2. The word "indolent" is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: تعریف داخل همان جمله آمده: «tumors that would never have become clinically apparent» → رشد بسیار کند. واژگان overdiagnosis همیشه با indolent همراه است.
questions.tip: indolent در متون انکولوژی = کم‌خطر و آهسته؛ این واژه در آزمون‌های قبلی بارها آمده است — حفظ کنید.

questions.q: 3. Why is supplemental MRI recommended for BRCA mutation carriers?
options: because MRI is cheaper than mammography
because dense tissue and earlier onset reduce the sensitivity of mammography in these women
because BRCA tumors do not appear on mammography at all
questions.explanation: «whose dense breast tissue and earlier disease onset reduce mammographic sensitivity». گزینه ۳ مطلق‌سازی غلط (کاهش حساسیت ≠ دیده‌نشدن مطلق).
questions.tip: پاساژهای غربالگری الگوی ثابت دارند: «در گروه پرخطر، تست مکمل به‌دلیل محدودیت تست اصلی» — این الگو را به خاطر بسپارید.

questions.q: 4. It can be inferred that breast self-examination lost prominence because:
options: it is too expensive for public programs
randomized trials did not show reduced mortality
questions.explanation: «randomized trials failed to demonstrate a mortality reduction» — عین متن. معیار طلایی ارزش‌گذاری هر آزمون غربالگری = کاهش مرگ‌ومیر در کارآزمایی.
questions.tip: در متون غربالگری، جمله «کارآزمایی تصادفی نشان داد/نشان نداد» همیشه سوژه سوال است.

questions.q: 5. The emerging paradigm described in the passage is:
options: uniform screening for all women at the same age
tailoring screening intensity and modality to individual risk
questions.explanation: پاراگراف پایانی: «Risk-stratified screening ... tailored to individual risk profiles» — گزینه ۱ برعکسِ one-size-fits-all است که متن آن را کنار می‌گذارد.
questions.tip: پاساژهای علمی جدید اغلب در جمله آخر «پارادایم نوظهور» را معرفی می‌کنند؛ اگر سوال آخر ریدینگ درباره آینده/روند باشد، جمله پایانی را ببینید.

english.section_title_fa: زبان تخصصی — بخش دوم: آناتومی پستان، اپیدمیولوژی و درمان‌های نوین

readings.title: The Normal Breast and Benign Breast Disease
readings.source: بر اساس فصل: The Normal Breast and Benign Diseases of the Breast
readings.passage: The functional unit of the female breast is the terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU), which consists of the terminal duct and its associated alveoli. The entire ductal system is lined by two cell layers: an inner layer of epithelial cells responsible for milk secretion and an outer layer of myoepithelial cells whose contractile properties propel secretions toward the nipple. This dual layering has diagnostic significance, because invasive carcinomas are characterized by the loss of myoepithelial cells, whereas benign in situ proliferations retain them. Most benign breast conditions reflect exaggerated responses of the TDLU to hormonal stimulation. Fibroadenomas, the most common benign neoplasms in young women, are composed of both stromal and epithelial components and typically present as mobile, well-circumscribed masses. Sclerosing adenosis, a proliferation of distorted acini within fibrotic stroma, may mimic carcinoma both clinically and radiologically, frequently containing microcalcifications that warrant biopsy. Fat necrosis, often following trauma or surgery, produces a firm irregular mass that can closely resemble malignancy. Similarly, chronic mastitis and inflammatory carcinoma may be indistinguishable on clinical grounds alone, underscoring the essential role of biopsy in the evaluation of any dominant breast mass. Ectopic breast tissue, most commonly in the axilla, may enlarge during pregnancy and raise unfounded concern for metastasis.
vocab: واحد ترمینال دکتال-لوبولار؛ واحد عملکردی پستان
سلول‌های میواپیتلیال؛ لایه بیرونی با خاصیت انقباضی
درجا؛ محدود به محل خود بدون تهاجم
اسکلروزانگ آدنوزیس؛ تکثیر آسینی‌های بدشکل با استروم فیبروتیک
میکروکلسیفیکاسیون‌ها؛ ریز رسوبات کلسیم در ماموگرافی
نکروز چربی؛ پس از تروما، شبیه بدخیمی

questions.q: 1. Why is the two-cell-layer structure of the ductal system diagnostically important?
options: because loss of myoepithelial cells marks invasive carcinoma while benign in situ lesions retain them
because epithelial cells are absent in benign tumors
because the layers determine the side of the tumor
questions.explanation: جمله سوم صریحاً: «invasive carcinomas are characterized by the loss of myoepithelial cells, whereas benign in situ proliferations retain them» — نکته هیستوپاتولوژیک کلیدی.
questions.tip: عبارت diagnostic significance در متن علامت است که جمله بعد، سوژه سوال است.

questions.q: 2. Which benign lesion most likely requires biopsy because of its radiologic appearance?
questions.explanation: «Sclerosing adenosis ... may mimic carcinoma both clinically and radiologically, frequently containing microcalcifications that warrant biopsy»؛ mimic carcinoma = شبیه بدخیمی → نیاز به بیوپسی.
questions.tip: دو واژه mimic و warrant را بشناسید: mimic = شبیه‌سازی بدخیمی؛ warrant = ایجاب کردن/موجب شدن (اقدام).

questions.q: 3. The word "propel" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: سلول میواپیتلیال با انقباض ترشحات را به سمت نوک پستان «به جلو می‌راند». ریشه فیزیکی propel = پیش‌رانندگی.
questions.tip: همیشه وظیفه بیولوژیک ساختار را در توضیح واژه لحاظ کنید: myo- (عضله) + propel (راندن).

questions.q: 4. It can be inferred that a firm irregular breast mass:
options: may result from fat necrosis and still require biopsy for clarification
questions.explanation: «Fat necrosis ... produces a firm irregular mass that can closely resemble malignancy» + «underscoring the essential role of biopsy» → استنباط: بیوپسی لازم است حتی اگر علت خوش‌خیم محتمل باشد. گزینه always مطلق و غلط.
questions.tip: استنباط معکوس: هرچه «همیشه/هرگز» دارد غلط؛ هرچه با منطق احتیاط بالینی (بیوپسی/پیگیری) سازگار است درست.

questions.q: 5. Enlarging axillary breast tissue during pregnancy:
options: is a typical behavior of ectopic breast tissue and usually benign
questions.explanation: جمله آخر: «Ectopic breast tissue, most commonly in the axilla, may enlarge during pregnancy and raise unfounded concern for metastasis» — unfounded = بی‌پایه؛ یعنی نگرانی بی‌مورد است.
questions.tip: واژه unfounded/baseless در متن یعنی متن خودش نگرانی را رد می‌کند — گزینه‌های تشدیدکننده نگرانی غلط‌اند.

readings.title: Cancer Epidemiology in Iran: A National Profile
readings.source: بر اساس: GLOBOCAN Fact Sheet — Iran (Islamic Republic of), 2022
readings.passage: According to the most recent global estimates, approximately 137,000 new cancer cases and 87,000 cancer deaths occur annually in Iran. Cancer of the stomach ranks first in men, followed by prostate and lung cancer, whereas breast cancer is by far the most common malignancy in women, followed by stomach and colorectal cancers. The age-standardized incidence rate in men (about 168 per 100,000) exceeds that in women (about 129 per 100,000), and the cumulative risk of developing cancer before age 75 approaches 18 percent in men. Several features distinguish the Iranian cancer profile from Western patterns. First, the relatively young age structure of the population means that a substantial proportion of patients are diagnosed during their productive years, amplifying the societal burden of disease. Second, infection-related malignancies such as gastric cancer—linked to Helicobacter pylori prevalence—remain prominent, reflecting the epidemiologic transition in which infections and lifestyle-related cancers coexist. Third, hereditary cancer research has gained momentum: population studies of breast cancer have documented a notable frequency of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations among high-risk families, and national programs for thalassemia prevention have demonstrated that community-based genetic screening can substantially reduce the birth incidence of a severe hereditary disease. Public health planners therefore confront a dual challenge: expanding early detection infrastructure for common cancers while integrating genetic counseling services into the primary health care system that Iran has long been recognized for.
vocab: نرخ استانداردشده سنی؛ برای مقایسه بین جمعیت‌ها
ریسک تجمعی؛ خطر تجمع تا سن مشخص
بروز؛ موارد جدید در واحد زمان
گذار اپیدمیولوژیک؛ هم‌زمانی بیماری‌های عفونی و مزمن
شیوع تولد؛ فراوانی تولد نوزادان مبتلا
مراقبت‌های اولیه سلامت؛ نقطه قوت نظام سلامت ایران

questions.q: 1. What is the most common cancer in Iranian women according to the passage?
questions.explanation: «breast cancer is by far the most common malignancy in women» — by far = با اختلاف زیاد. stomach و colorectal رتبه‌های بعدی‌اند.
questions.tip: در جداول توصیفی، قیدهای رتبه‌بندی (first, followed by, by far) را زیر خط بکشید؛ سوال رتبه‌بندی بسیار رایج است.

questions.q: 2. The passage attributes the prominence of gastric cancer in Iran partly to:
questions.explanation: «infection-related malignancies such as gastric cancer—linked to Helicobacter pylori prevalence—remain prominent» — dash دومیکروبی عامل را روشن می‌کند.
questions.tip: داش‌های توضیحی (—...—) در ریدینگهای آزمون معمولاً حاوی پاسخ‌اند؛ از آن‌ها نپرید.

questions.q: 3. The phrase "amplifying the societal burden" suggests that:
options: young patients impose greater indirect costs because illness strikes during productive years
cancer only affects retired people in Iran
questions.explanation: منطق متن: ساختار سنی جوان + تشخیص در سال‌های بارور → بار اجتماعی (اقتصادی/خانوادگی) بزرگ‌تر. گزینه ۲ و ۳ با متن ناسازگار؛ ۴ برعکسِ «relatively young age structure».
questions.tip: پیامدهای اجتماعی بیماری در سوالات استنباطی، معمولاً حول بار اقتصادی/کاهش نیروی کار می‌چرخد.

questions.q: 4. The thalassemia prevention program is mentioned as evidence that:
options: genetic screening cannot work at the community level
community-based genetic screening can markedly reduce the birth incidence of a hereditary disease
questions.explanation: «national programs for thalassemia prevention have demonstrated that community-based genetic screening can substantially reduce the birth incidence» — demonstrate = نشان دادن؛ مثال تاریخی موفقیت ژنتیک عمومی در ایران.
questions.tip: هرگاه متن یک برنامه ملی را به‌عنوان «demonstrated that...» بیاورد، دقیقاً همان گزاره بعد از that گزینه صحیح است.

questions.q: 5. The "dual challenge" faced by planners consists of:
options: reducing the population and banning screening
expanding early detection for common cancers and integrating genetic counseling into primary care
questions.explanation: جمله پایانی دو جزء چالش را با while به هم پیوند می‌دهد؛ گزینه صحیح باید هر دو جزء را داشته باشد.
questions.tip: در سوالاتی که «دو جزئی» هستند، گزینه‌ای که فقط یک جزء را می‌گوید (مثلاً فقط غربالگری) ناقص و غلط است.

readings.title: CRISPR Base Editing: From Bench to Approved Therapy
readings.source: بر اساس پیشرفت‌های ۲۰۲۳-۲۰۲۵: تأیید exagamglogene autotemcel و موج ویرایش پایه
readings.passage: In late 2023, regulatory authorities approved the first therapy based on CRISPR gene editing, marking a milestone in the treatment of sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia. The treatment, known as exagamglogene autotemcel, does not repair the causative mutation directly. Instead, it edits hematopoietic stem cells collected from the patient so that a precisely targeted breakpoint is created in an enhancer of the BCL11A gene specific to erythroid cells. Disrupting this regulatory element reactivates fetal hemoglobin production, which compensates for the defective adult hemoglobin. Because the edited cells are the patient's own, immunological rejection is avoided, although recipients must still undergo conditioning chemotherapy to make room in the marrow. Parallel to nuclease-based editing, a quieter revolution has occurred with base editing, a CRISPR-derived technology that converts one DNA letter directly into another without cutting both strands of the double helix. By avoiding double-strand breaks, base editors substantially reduce the risk of unwanted rearrangements, and investigational therapies have already achieved functional correction of hemoglobinopathies in early trials. Nevertheless, important limitations persist: editing efficiency varies among stem-cell clones, long-term safety data remain limited to a few years of follow-up, off-target effects—though greatly reduced—cannot be excluded entirely, and the current cost places the therapy beyond the reach of most health systems where these diseases are most prevalent. Access, rather than science, is now widely regarded as the principal barrier between gene editing and global equity.
vocab: ویرایش ژن؛ تغییر هدفمند توالی DNA
شیمی‌درمانی آماده‌سازی؛ خالی‌کردن جای مغز استخوان
ویرایش پایه؛ تبدیل مستقیم یک نوکلئوتید بدون برش دو‌رشته
اثرات خارج از هدف؛ ویرایش ناخواسته جایگاه‌های دیگر

questions.q: 1. How does exagamglogene autotemcel exert its therapeutic effect?
options: by directly repairing the sickle mutation
by disrupting a BCL11A erythroid enhancer to reactivate fetal hemoglobin
by replacing bone marrow with donor cells
by delivering the editing enzymes intravenously without cell collection
questions.explanation: «it edits ... a breakpoint ... in an enhancer of the BCL11A gene specific to erythroid cells. Disrupting this regulatory element reactivates fetal hemoglobin» — هدف غیرمستقیم BCL11A است نه خود جهش.
questions.tip: مکانیسم‌های درمانی جدید را با «هدف» و «اثر» دو ستونه یادداشت کنید؛ سوال mechanism معمولاً یکی از این دو را جابه‌جا می‌کند.

questions.q: 2. The main advantage of base editing over nuclease editing, as stated, is:
options: avoidance of double-strand breaks and thus fewer unwanted rearrangements
no requirement for a guide RNA
questions.explanation: «By avoiding double-strand breaks, base editors substantially reduce the risk of unwanted rearrangements» — گزینه‌های دیگر در متن نیستند.
questions.tip: در تکنولوژی‌های نو، جمله‌ای که با By avoiding/By reducing شروع می‌شود معمولاً «مزیت» را می‌سازد و مستقیماً سوال می‌شود.

questions.q: 3. The word "conditioning" refers to:
questions.explanation: «must still undergo conditioning chemotherapy to make room in the marrow» — تعریف داخل جمله آمده است.
questions.tip: واژگان تخصصی درمان (conditioning) در پاساژهای ژن‌درمانی همیشه با توضیح همراه می‌آید؛ جمله را تا انتها بخوانید.

questions.q: 4. Which limitation is NOT mentioned in the passage?
options: complete absence of any therapeutic effect in all patients
questions.explanation: سه مورد اول صریحاً ذکر شده‌اند؛ «absence of any therapeutic effect» نه در متن است و نه با تأیید درمان سازگار است — گزینه مطلق و غلط.
questions.tip: سوال NOT mentioned: گزینه با ادعای مطلقِ منفی درباره اثربخشی، معمولاً جواب است چون متن درباره کارایی مثبت صحبت می‌کند.

questions.q: 5. The final sentence implies that the foremost obstacle to global impact of gene editing is:
questions.explanation: «Access, rather than science, is now widely regarded as the principal barrier» — ساختار X rather than Y به‌طور مستقیم پاسخ را می‌دهد.
questions.tip: ساختار rather than در جمله پایانی = مقایسه مستقیم دو عامل؛ یکی برجسته می‌شود و همان جواب سوال است.

readings.title: Synthetic Lethality: PARP Inhibitors and DNA Repair
readings.source: بر اساس مباحث روز: PARP inhibition in homologous recombination deficiency
readings.passage: The concept of synthetic lethality arises when simultaneous defects in two genes or pathways kill a cell, whereas a defect in either one alone is tolerable. Tumor cells lacking functional BRCA1 or BRCA2 cannot perform homologous recombination, the high-fidelity pathway that repairs double-strand DNA breaks. They survive, however, by leaning on alternative repair mechanisms, particularly the base excision and single-strand break repair pathways in which the enzyme poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, or PARP, plays a central role. Pharmacological inhibitors of PARP exploit this dependence: by trapping PARP enzymes at sites of single-strand damage, they prevent replication forks from proceeding, converting unrepaired single-strand lesions into lethal double-strand breaks. In homologous recombination-proficient cells, such breaks would be repaired accurately and the cell would survive; in BRCA-deficient tumor cells, they accumulate catastrophically. This mechanism explains the remarkable selectivity of PARP inhibitors for tumors with germline BRCA mutations, while normal tissues are largely spared. Clinical trials established drugs of this class as effective maintenance therapy in ovarian and breast cancers associated with BRCA mutations or other forms of homologous recombination deficiency, and assays that quantify genomic scarring—cumulative signatures of past repair failure—are now used to identify additional patients who may benefit. Resistance, nonetheless, emerges through several routes, including restoration of homologous recombination by secondary BRCA mutations, replication fork protection, and drug efflux, motivating combination strategies that pair PARP inhibitors with agents targeting these escape pathways.
vocab: مرگ‌ومیری مصنوعی/ترکیبی؛ نقص هم‌زمان دو مسیر
نوترکیبی همولوگ؛ ترمیم دقیق شکست‌های دو‌رشته
زخم‌های ژنومی؛ نشانه‌های تجمعی نقص ترمیم
درمان نگهدارنده پس از پاسخ اولیه

questions.q: 1. Synthetic lethality, as defined in the passage, requires that:
options: each single defect is independently lethal
only the combination of both defects is lethal
both genes are on the same chromosome
the cell lacks all DNA repair pathways
questions.explanation: «when simultaneous defects in two genes or pathways kill a cell, whereas a defect in either one alone is tolerable» — گزینه ۱ دقیقاً برعکس تعریف است.
questions.tip: تعاریف علمی در جمله اول پاساژ اغلب سوژه سوال تعریف می‌شوند؛ کلمات whereas/while را دقت کنید.

questions.q: 2. How do PARP inhibitors kill BRCA-deficient cells specifically?
options: by trapping PARP at single-strand damage, converting lesions into lethal double-strand breaks the cell cannot repair
by directly cutting both DNA strands
by inhibiting transcription of PARP mRNA only
questions.explanation: زنجیره مکانیسمی متن: trapping PARP ← fork stalling ← conversion به DSB ← سلول HR-deficient نمی‌ترمیم ← مرگ. سلول نرمال با HR ترمیم می‌کند و زنده می‌ماند → selectivity.
questions.tip: پاساژهای فارماکولوژیک مولکولی را به‌صورت زنجیره علت-معلول یادداشت کنید؛ سوال mechanism همیشه یکی از حلقه‌ها را می‌پرسد.

questions.q: 3. The term "genomic scarring" is used to describe:
options: cumulative mutational signatures of past homologous recombination failure
questions.explanation: داش توضیحی بعد از عبارت تعریف را می‌دهد: «cumulative signatures of past repair failure» — کاربرد: شناسایی بیمارانِ کانداد PARPi حتی بدون جهش BRCA.
questions.tip: اصطلاحات بسته‌بندی‌شده (scarring, synthetic lethality, trapping) همیشه در متن تعریف می‌شوند؛ تعریف را حفظ کنید نه فقط واژه را.

questions.q: 4. Which mechanism of resistance is mentioned?
options: loss of the drug target's gene
restoration of homologous recombination through secondary mutations
questions.explanation: «Resistance ... emerges through ... restoration of homologous recombination by secondary BRCA mutations, replication fork protection, and drug efflux» — سه سازوکار ذکر شده؛ گزینه ۱ یکی از آن‌هاست.
questions.tip: سوالات مقاومت دارویی: لیست کوتاه سازوکارها در متن را شماره‌گذارید؛ طراح یکی را برمی‌دارد و سه گزینه از خارج متن می‌سازد.

questions.q: 5. The overall tone of the passage toward PARP inhibitors is best described as:
options: informative and balanced, acknowledging efficacy and resistance
questions.explanation: متن هم «remarkable selectivity» و اثربخشی را می‌گوید و هم «Resistance, nonetheless, emerges» را — لحن متعادل علمی. گزینه‌های یک‌سویه غلط‌اند.
questions.tip: لحن پاساژهای علمی استاندارد تقریباً همیشه «balanced/informative» است؛ در آزمون، گزینه balanced معمولاً صحیح است مگر متن آشکارا تبلیغی باشد.

readings.title: Liquid Biopsy and Molecular Residual Disease
readings.source: بر اساس مقالات ۲۰۲۴-۲۰۲۶ درباره ctDNA و MRD
readings.passage: The term liquid biopsy refers to the analysis of tumor-derived molecules—most commonly circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)—obtained from a simple blood draw rather than from an invasive tissue biopsy. ctDNA fragments, typically around 160 base pairs in length, enter the circulation through the apoptosis of tumor cells and can be detected by deeply sequencing plasma DNA. One of the most consequential applications is the assessment of molecular residual disease (MRD) after apparently curative surgery. Patients in whom ctDNA remains detectable postoperatively have a very high probability of radiographic relapse, often months before conventional imaging reveals any abnormality; conversely, patients who test negative have a substantially lower recurrence risk. This predictive window has encouraged adaptive treatment trials in which adjuvant chemotherapy is escalated for ctDNA-positive patients and de-escalated for ctDNA-negative patients, sparing many from unnecessary toxicity. Despite this promise, important constraints apply. Detection sensitivity depends on tumor burden, location, and shedding biology; certain tumors, notably some brain malignancies, release little DNA across the blood–brain barrier. Assays must be exquisitely specific, because clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP)—age-related expansion of mutated blood clones—frequently generates DNA variants in plasma that mimic tumor mutations and can cause false-positive results unless appropriately filtered. Standardization across laboratories remains incomplete, and guidelines accordingly recommend MRD testing within clinical trials or with careful counseling until prospective evidence matures.
vocab: بیوپسی مایع؛ نمونه‌برداری خونی به‌جای بافت
بیماری باقیمانده مولکولی پس از درمان
خون‌سازی کلونال؛ کلون‌های جهش‌یافته خونی مرتبط با سن

questions.q: 1. What is the typical length of ctDNA fragments mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: «typically around 160 base pairs in length» — عدد مشخص؛ گزینه‌ها با جابه‌جایی اعشار طراحی شده‌اند.
questions.tip: اعداد را با دقت بخوانید؛ طراحان معمولاً ۰ اضافه یا کم می‌کنند (60/160/1600).

questions.q: 2. Postoperative detection of ctDNA implies that:
options: relapse is very likely, often preceding radiographic evidence
questions.explanation: «Patients in whom ctDNA remains detectable postoperatively have a very high probability of radiographic relapse, often months before conventional imaging reveals any abnormality» — MRD مثبت = پیش‌آگهی بد.
questions.tip: منطق MRD: ctDNA پس از جراحی = سلول توموری میکروسکوپی باقیمانده = عود آینده. این زنجیره را بدانید.

questions.q: 3. According to the passage, adaptive trials based on ctDNA results aim to:
options: give the same chemotherapy to all patients
escalate treatment for ctDNA-positive and spare ctDNA-negative patients from unnecessary toxicity
delay treatment until relapse appears on imaging
questions.explanation: «adjuvant chemotherapy is escalated for ctDNA-positive patients and de-escalated for ctDNA-negative patients, sparing many from unnecessary toxicity» — شخصی‌سازی درمان کمکی.
questions.tip: روان مطالب oncology دقیق: «adaptive/escalate/de-escalate» سه واژه کلیدی درمان شخصی‌شده‌اند.

questions.q: 4. Why does CHIP threaten the accuracy of liquid biopsy?
options: it destroys ctDNA in the tube
it produces plasma variants that resemble tumor mutations, causing false positives
questions.explanation: «clonal hematopoiesis ... frequently generates DNA variants in plasma that mimic tumor mutations and can cause false-positive results unless appropriately filtered» — تقلید از جهش تومور.
questions.tip: CHIP در سوالات اخیر همه‌جا هست: تعریف آن (کلون خونی جهش‌یافته وابسته سن) و مشکلش (مثبت کاذب) را یک‌جا حفظ کنید.

questions.q: 5. Which tumor type is noted as poorly suited to ctDNA detection?
questions.explanation: «certain tumors, notably some brain malignancies, release little DNA across the blood–brain barrier» — سد خونی-مغزی مانع آزادسازی DNA است.
questions.tip: هرگز جواب‌ها را از دانش عمومی حدس نزنید؛ «brain/BBB» فقط به این دلیل در متن بود که سوژۀ سوال شود.

readings.title: Polygenic Risk Scores in Population Screening
readings.source: بر اساس مقالات ۲۰۲۴-۲۰۲۶ درباره PRS و غربالگری ریسک‌محور
readings.passage: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued hundreds of common variants that individually exert tiny effects on disease susceptibility. A polygenic risk score (PRS) aggregates these effects into a single number that positions an individual along a continuum of inherited risk. For breast cancer, women in the top percentile of the score distribution face a several-fold higher lifetime risk than the population average, comparable in magnitude to some moderate-penetrance monogenic variants. This predictive capacity has fueled proposals for risk-stratified screening: women at high polygenic risk might begin mammography earlier or add annual magnetic resonance imaging, whereas women at low risk might safely delay the onset of screening, reducing overdiagnosis and conserving resources. Formidable obstacles, however, separate theory from implementation. The overwhelming majority of underlying association data derive from populations of European ancestry, and score performance degrades—sometimes dramatically—when applied to other ancestries, a problem known as reduced portability or transferability. Efforts to remedy this include multi-ancestry meta-analysis, larger local reference panels, and ancestry-specific score calibration, all of which require sustained international collaboration and data sharing. Additional concerns include limited communication of probabilistic results to patients, the potential for anxiety or false reassurance, and interactions with non-genetic risk factors such as mammographic density and hormonal exposures. Current guidelines therefore position PRS as an adjunct rather than a replacement for established risk models, pending evidence from prospective interventional studies that stratified screening improves outcomes without widening health inequities.
vocab: انتقال‌پذیری؛ عملکرد مدل در جمعیت دیگر
کالیبراسیون؛ تطبیق پیش‌بینی با ریسک واقعی
مکمل؛ ابزار کمکی در کنار روش اصلی

questions.q: 1. A PRS is best described as:
options: a diagnostic test for active disease
an aggregate of many small-effect variants summarizing inherited risk
questions.explanation: «aggregates these effects into a single number that positions an individual along a continuum of inherited risk» — خلاصه‌ساز ریسک، نه تشخیص بیماری موجود.
questions.tip: PRS را با «رتبه‌بندی ریسک» ترجمه کنید نه «تشخیص» — گزینه‌های تشخیصی همیشه انحرافی‌اند.

questions.q: 2. In risk-stratified screening, women with low polygenic risk might:
options: safely delay screening onset, reducing overdiagnosis
questions.explanation: «women at low risk might safely delay the onset of screening, reducing overdiagnosis and conserving resources» — منطق دو‌طرفه تخصیص منابع.
questions.tip: دو سمت طیف ریسک را جدول کنید: high → earlier/MRI؛ low → delay — سوال معمولاً یک سمت را می‌پرسد.

questions.q: 3. The term "transferability" refers to:
options: how well a score performs when applied to ancestries other than those in which it was developed
the ability to transfer patients between hospitals
questions.explanation: «score performance degrades ... when applied to other ancestries, a problem known as reduced portability or transferability» — تعریف داخل جمله.
questions.tip: مفاهیم bias/عدالت در ژنومیکس جمعیتی از موضوعات محبوب جدید است؛ تعریف transferability را حفظ کنید.

questions.q: 4. Which strategy is mentioned as a remedy for the ancestry problem?
questions.explanation: «Efforts to remedy this include multi-ancestry meta-analysis, larger local reference panels, and ancestry-specific score calibration».
questions.tip: سوالات «solution/remedy»: جملات شامل Efforts to remedy/include را هدف بگیرید.

questions.q: 5. According to current guidelines mentioned in the passage, PRS should be regarded as:
options: a replacement for established risk models
a screening test for all newborns
a tool only for researchers, never clinicians
questions.explanation: «position PRS as an adjunct rather than a replacement for established risk models» — همان ساختار X rather than Y.
questions.tip: adjunct = مکمل؛ در متون راهنمایی، وضعیت نوظهورها تقریباً همیشه «adjunct pending evidence» است.

readings.title: Personalized Neoantigen Cancer Vaccines
readings.source: بر اساس فاز ۲b/۳ mRNA-4157 و پیشرفت‌های ۲۰۲۴-۲۰۲۶
readings.passage: Unlike infectious disease vaccines, which present identical antigens to an entire population, personalized cancer vaccines are manufactured for a single patient from the unique mutations of that patient's tumor. The workflow begins with whole-exome and RNA sequencing of tumor and normal tissue, followed by computational pipelines that nominate candidate neoantigens—mutated peptides predicted to bind the patient's human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules and to be recognized by T lymphocytes. Twenty to thirty-four selected epitopes are then encoded into a delivery vehicle, most prominently messenger RNA encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles, the same platform proven at global scale by COVID-19 vaccines. In randomized studies of resected high-risk melanoma, the combination of an individualized neoantigen vaccine with the immune checkpoint inhibitor pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival compared with pembrolizumab alone, and similar strategies are advancing in pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal tumors. Formidable logistical hurdles nonetheless remain: manufacturing each patient's bespoke product takes weeks, requires deep tumor sequencing of sufficient quality, and depends on reliable algorithms whose predictions of immunogenicity remain imperfect. Tumors with low mutation burden furnish few candidate neoantigens, limiting applicability, and glucocorticoid use around infusion has been associated with diminished immune responses. Whether the approach will extend beyond mutation-rich tumors, and whether health systems can absorb its cost, are questions that ongoing Phase III trials are now positioned to answer.
vocab: نئوآنتی‌ژن؛ پپتید نوظهور از جهش تومور
اپیتوپ؛ بخش آنتی‌ژن قابل شناسایی توسط ایمنی
بقای بدون عود؛ نقطه پایانی کارآزمایی
سفارشی‌دوز؛ ساخت اختصاصی برای یک فرد

questions.q: 1. What distinguishes personalized cancer vaccines from conventional vaccines?
options: they use killed whole tumor cells
each vaccine is built from the unique mutations of an individual patient's tumor
they are identical across the population
questions.explanation: «Unlike infectious disease vaccines, which present identical antigens to an entire population, personalized cancer vaccines are manufactured for a single patient from the unique mutations...» — جمله اول تقابل را کامل می‌کند.
questions.tip: جمله اول پاساژ با Unlike شروع می‌شود → تفاوت دو مفهوم؛ در سوال تفاوت، همین جمله جواب است.

questions.q: 2. A candidate neoantigen must satisfy which prediction requirement?
options: binding to the patient's HLA molecules and recognition by T lymphocytes
questions.explanation: «mutated peptides predicted to bind the patient's HLA molecules and to be recognized by T lymphocytes» — دو شرط: اتصال HLA و شناسایی T.
questions.tip: پپتید-اتصال HLA-شناسایی T لمفوسیت سه‌گانه ثابت ایمیونولوژی واکسن است.

questions.q: 3. The vaccine platform highlighted in the passage is:
questions.explanation: «most prominently messenger RNA encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles, the same platform proven at global scale by COVID-19 vaccines».
questions.tip: پیوند فناوری واکسن کووید با واکسن سرطان نکته محبوب متن‌های جدید است.

questions.q: 4. Tumors with low mutation burden are a challenge because:
options: they grow too fast to sequence
they do not respond to pembrolizumab under any circumstances
questions.explanation: «Tumors with low mutation burden furnish few candidate neoantigens, limiting applicability» — furnish = فراهم‌کردن.
questions.tip: furnish/provide/yield واژه‌های مترادف «فراهم‌آوردن»اند؛ در سوال علت، شرط کمبود ماده اولیه (neoantigen) را دنبال کنید.

questions.q: 5. The passage indicates that Phase III trials will primarily clarify:
options: the mechanism of lipid nanoparticle formation
broader applicability, outcomes, and affordability for health systems
questions.explanation: جمله پایانی دو پرسش باز را نام می‌برد: تعمیم به تومورهای کم‌جهش و هزینه/جذب توسط نظام سلامت — دقیقاً محور فاز ۳.
questions.tip: جمله پایانی با Whether...or whether ساختار «پرسش‌های باز آینده» می‌سازد؛ سوالی درباره نقش فاز ۳ از همین می‌آید.

readings.title: Artificial Intelligence in Structural Genomics
readings.passage: For half a century, determining the three-dimensional structure of a protein required years of laboratory work using X-ray crystallography or nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Deep-learning systems have now largely overturned that bottleneck. AlphaFold, first demonstrated at an international structure-prediction contest, predicts protein structures from amino acid sequences with accuracy approaching experimental methods for a large fraction of targets, and its successor extends predictions to complexes of proteins with DNA, RNA, and small ligands. Structural biologists now routinely consult predicted models when designing experiments, docking studies, and mutagenesis strategies, and databases containing hundreds of millions of predicted structures have become public resources. The impact on rare disease genetics is particularly noteworthy: for variants of uncertain significance in genes lacking structural data, predicted models permit researchers to map substitutions onto three-dimensional space, distinguish those disrupting buried hydrophobic cores or catalytic residues from benign surface changes, and thereby prioritize variants for functional assays. Enthusiasm must nevertheless be tempered by genuine limitations. Predicted confidence varies across regions; intrinsically disordered segments, alternative conformations, and dynamic complexes remain difficult; and ligand-binding pockets—central to drug discovery—may be modeled with less reliability than protein backbones. Nor does a structure, predicted or experimental, by itself explain a biological mechanism; integration with biochemical, genetic, and clinical data remains indispensable. Within these boundaries, machine-learning structure prediction has shifted from a computational curiosity to an everyday instrument of molecular biology and medical genetics.
vocab: بلورشناسی پرتو ایکس؛ روش تعیین ساختار
داکینگ؛ شبیه‌سازی اتصال لیگاند به پروتئین
در嫁给 بی‌نظم ذاتی؛ بخش‌های بدون ساختار ثابت

questions.q: 1. The main contribution of AlphaFold described in the passage is:
options: predicting protein structures from sequence at near-experimental accuracy for many targets
questions.explanation: «predicts protein structures from amino acid sequences with accuracy approaching experimental methods for a large fraction of targets» — گزینه ۱ مطلق‌سازی غلط است؛ متن گزینه ۳/۴ را نمی‌گوید.
questions.tip: درباره AI همیشه مراقب گزینه‌های اغراق‌آمیز (replace all/cure/directly) باشید؛ متن‌های علمی محتاط‌اند.

questions.q: 2. How do predicted structures aid rare disease genetics?
options: by mapping missense variants onto 3D space to distinguish structure-disrupting from benign changes
questions.explanation: «permit researchers to map substitutions onto three-dimensional space, distinguish those disrupting buried hydrophobic cores or catalytic residues from benign surface changes, and thereby prioritize variants» — کاربرد VUS تفسیری.
questions.tip: پیوند AI-VUS یکی از داغ‌ترین موضوعات ژنتیک بالینی جدید است؛ جمله‌اش را در متن هدف بگیرید.

questions.q: 3. Which aspect is described as modeled less reliably?
questions.explanation: «ligand-binding pockets—central to drug discovery—may be modeled with less reliability than protein backbones».
questions.tip: مقایسه‌های less/more reliable را علامت بزنید؛ سوال مقایسه‌ای می‌آید.

questions.q: 4. The phrase "tempered by genuine limitations" indicates that the author:
options: presents a balanced view acknowledging both value and constraints
questions.explanation: temper = تعدیل‌کردن؛ نویسنده بعد از ستایش، محدودیت‌های واقعی را فهرست می‌کند → لحن متعادل علمی.
questions.tip: temper/moderate/qualify هم‌خانواده‌اند: «تعادل‌دهی به ادعا» — نشان لحن balanced.

questions.q: 5. The passage concludes that machine-learning prediction now functions as:
options: an everyday instrument of molecular biology and medical genetics
questions.explanation: جمله آخر: «has shifted from a computational curiosity to an everyday instrument of molecular biology and medical genetics» — همان ساختار from X to Y.
questions.tip: جمله پایانی از X to Y تقابل گذشته/حاضر را می‌سازد؛ سوالی درباره وضعیت فعلی، بازتاب مستقیم Y است.
